source.title: 15 Years of Lightroom: My top 10 SECRETS
source.author: Serge Ramelli (photoserge.com)
source.url_hint: YouTube / photoserge.com tutorial (Serge Ramelli); frames grabbed from a 1280x720 screen recording

note: Trimmed copy of the photoserge lesson notes (no images, timestamps or diff stats). Used as few-shot hints for the planner prompts and as the reference for the lesson steps.
general_tips: Fix exposure (tone, black/white points) before white balance and colour work.
Use the clipping view (Alt/Option while dragging Blacks/Whites) to set black and white points: about 1-2% clipping for colour images, about 5% for B&W.
Keep brush dodge/burn subtle: within about +/-0.5 EV, Feather 100, Flow/Density around 70, and build up gradually.
Decide the story first, then remove distractions and use crop and vignettes/gradients to direct the eye to the subject.

examples.title: Paris sunset over the Seine - finding the right crop
examples.goal: Make one photo work for different outputs, with deliberate composition instead of the camera's native 3:2 frame.

edits.reason: 16:9 fits screens, TVs and YouTube/desktop viewing

edits.value: horizon on the lower rule-of-thirds line (about 1/3 sky, 2/3 water)
edits.reason: Rule-of-thirds placement is more dynamic than a centred horizon and gives weight to the colourful reflection
4:5 takes up the most space in vertical social feeds (Instagram/Facebook)

darktable_modules: crop (aspect: 16:9 or 4:5, guides: rule of thirds)
rotate and perspective (if the horizon needs levelling)
examples.darktable_equivalent: crop module: set the aspect to 16:9 (or 4:5 with portrait orientation) and turn on the rule-of-thirds guide overlay. This maps 1:1 to Lightroom's crop.

examples.title: Rocky cove at dusk - black and white point baseline
examples.goal: Set a proper tonal baseline (true black and white points, opened shadows) before any creative colour work.

edits.reason: Open up the very dark rocks and foreground
Protect the sky and the moon while the image gets brighter
Set a true black point: hold Alt/Option for the clipping view and stop when only 1-2% of the image shows as pure black
Set the white point by eye, so the brightest areas reach near-white without clipping

darktable_modules: sigmoid or filmic rgb (white/black relative exposure)
examples.darktable_equivalent: exposure for the global brightness. tone equalizer: raise the -8 to -5 EV bands and lower the -2 to 0 EV bands (Shadows +100 / Highlights -100). Black and white points: filmic rgb or sigmoid (white/black relative exposure / contrast), or rgb levels. Use the clipping indicator (raw/gamut overexposed toggles) the way Lightroom uses Alt-drag. Darktable has no exact Alt-drag clipping-preview slider.

examples.title: Golden hour on the Seine - exposure first, then warmth and clean hues
examples.goal: Fix exposure first, then push warmth on purpose and clean up the sunset hues so the sky glows orange instead of green-yellow.

edits.reason: Recover detail at both ends of a high-contrast backlit scene
Set the black and white points (clipping view) to give a proper baseline before touching colour
Deliberately warmer than neutral to amplify the golden-hour mood (correct exposure first, then white balance)
Make the sunset hues richer

edits.value: Yellow about -47 (blurry panel at 05:26 suggests about Orange -14, Yellow -50, Green -39)
edits.reason: Shift yellows toward orange to remove the green cast that warm WB plus saturation gives the sky

darktable_modules: color equalizer (or color zones) for per-hue saturation and hue
examples.darktable_equivalent: exposure + tone equalizer (shadows/highlights), then filmic rgb/sigmoid for black/white points. Warmth: color calibration (CAT tab, raise the illuminant temperature / move the hue) or white balance with a higher temperature. Per-hue saturation: color equalizer, saturation tab (red/orange/yellow up). Hue shift: color equalizer hue tab (yellow toward orange). color zones (hue vs hue curve) is an older alternative.

examples.title: Brooklyn street / Manhattan Bridge - 'Alen Palander look'
examples.goal: A stylised warm-only, muted-cool, high-contrast street look.

edits.reason: Keep and boost warm tones (brick, van, lights)
Mute the cool tones so the image becomes warm-only (signature Palander style)
High-contrast, punchy look
Pull overall colour intensity back down after the contrast boost so it stays moody, not garish

darktable_modules: color balance rgb (vibrance, global saturation, contrast)
examples.darktable_equivalent: color equalizer saturation tab: raise red/orange/yellow and lower green/cyan/blue/purple/magenta nodes (or a color zones saturation curve). color balance rgb: contrast slider (or sigmoid contrast) for +67 contrast, and the global vibrance slider for vibrance -23. Note: color balance rgb vibrance is not the same algorithm as Lightroom's, so tune by eye.

examples.title: NYC Flatiron at night - same warm-only look on a night scene
examples.goal: Show that the warm-tones-only look transfers to night photography: cleaner, more cohesive colour.

edits.reason: Keep the warm city lights and clock glowing
Kill the blue/cyan/magenta colour noise of mixed street lighting
Add punch to the night scene

examples.darktable_equivalent: Same as example 4: color equalizer saturation per hue (warm up, cool down) and color balance rgb or sigmoid contrast.

examples.title: Iceland volcano (drone) - selective colour, only red stays
examples.goal: Selective colour: the eye goes straight to the one remaining colour, the red crater.

edits.reason: Keep and strengthen only the red lava/crater colour

edits.setting: Orange / Yellow / Green / Aqua / Blue / Purple / Magenta
edits.value: on screen: -100 for all (analysis said Orange +6, Yellow +9, Green -65, Aqua -61, Blue -65, Purple -66, Magenta -100)
edits.reason: Remove every other colour, leaving a black-and-white landscape with a red accent
Dramatic, graphic monochrome

darktable_modules: alternative: monochrome + parametric mask on hue
examples.darktable_equivalent: color equalizer: saturation -100% on every node except red (raise red). A more robust alternative is a monochrome (or color calibration gray tab) instance with a parametric mask on hue (exclude reds) plus feathering. Contrast: color balance rgb contrast or sigmoid.

examples.title: Paris river with street lamp - AI landscape masks
examples.goal: Treat each region (sky, buildings, trees, water, ground) separately to build depth, colour contrast and a clear focal point.

edits.reason: Darker, warmer, more magenta sky for a richer dusk mood
Brighten and crisp up the buildings so they read as the subject
Make the trees greener (less magenta cast)
Darker, bluer, smoother water so it doesn't compete and contrasts with the warm sky
Darken the cobblestones so the foreground is less distracting

darktable_modules: exposure, color balance rgb, color calibration, local contrast, sharpen / diffuse or sharpen, each with drawn and parametric masks
examples.darktable_equivalent: No direct equivalent: darktable has no AI 'Select Landscape' semantic masks. Make separate module instances (exposure, color balance rgb for warmth/tint, local contrast for clarity/texture, sharpen or diffuse or sharpen for sharpness/smoothing) and mask each one. Sky: parametric mask on lightness + blue/hue, refined with details threshold and guided filter. Water: drawn path/gradient + parametric. Buildings/ground: drawn paths or brush. Vegetation: parametric mask on green hue (color equalizer can also shift green directly). Expect much more manual work than Lightroom.

examples.title: Big Ben sunset from Westminster Bridge - remove distractions, crop, guide the eye
examples.goal: Simplify the scene and steer attention to the subject by removing distractions, re-framing and darkening the foreground.

edits.reason: Remove pedestrians and sensor dust that pull attention from the landmark

edits.value: 16:9, frame shifted up toward Big Ben
edits.reason: Cut the empty road and put more of the frame on the tower and sky
Darken the road/foreground so the eye moves up to Big Ben and the sky

examples.darktable_equivalent: retouch module (heal/clone brush and spot removal) for dust and people. No automatic people/dust detection, so it is manual work, and people on a railing are hard to heal. crop at 16:9. exposure instance at -0.68 EV with a drawn gradient mask from the bottom (or graduated density module).

examples.title: Paris street with Eiffel Tower at sunset - gradient intersected with sky
examples.goal: Add a graduated-filter effect to the sky only, without the typical side effect of darkening tall buildings.

edits.value: -0.85 / about -11 (panel at 13:10.5 reads -0.85; temp is low confidence)
edits.reason: Darken and slightly cool the top of the sky to add drama and keep the eye in the frame
Stop the gradient from darkening the buildings, which a plain gradient would also hit

darktable_modules: exposure (or graduated density) with drawn gradient + parametric mask combined
color calibration / color balance rgb for the slight cooling
examples.darktable_equivalent: exposure instance at about -0.85 EV with a drawn gradient from the top, combined (drawn & parametric) with a parametric mask selecting the sky (high lightness / blue-purple hue, details threshold + guided filter to refine edges). No AI sky mask, so the parametric mask stands in for 'Select Sky'. The cooling can be a white balance/color calibration tweak in the same masked instance.

examples.title: Studio male portrait - background glow behind the subject
examples.goal: Separate the subject from the backdrop with a subtle glow behind the head and shoulders, like a background light.

edits.reason: Create a light pool on the backdrop
Trick: on a studio shot, 'Select Sky' picks the plain backdrop, so the glow stays off the subject

darktable_modules: exposure with drawn ellipse mask combined with a parametric/inverted subject mask
examples.darktable_equivalent: exposure instance at about +1.2 to +2.2 EV (tune by eye) with a drawn ellipse mask (large feather) behind the subject, minus the subject: combine with an inverted drawn path/brush around the person, or a parametric mask on lightness/chroma if the backdrop is distinct enough. No AI subject/sky mask in darktable, so this is manual.

examples.title: Tuscany B&W landscape - dodge and burn for 3D depth
examples.goal: Zone-system dodge and burn: create 3D depth and a clear light path leading to the cypress trees in the centre.

edits.setting: Exposure (top / upper half / top edge / bottom-left / bottom-right)
edits.reason: Darken the edges and corners (a hand-built vignette) to keep the eye in the centre

edits.tool: Masking > Radial Gradient over trees, intersected with Sky
edits.reason: Glow in the sky behind the cypress row so the trees pop

edits.value: +0.44 on centre field and inner clouds
edits.reason: Lift the light where the eye should go, sculpting the light

edits.value: -0.34 / 100 / 99 / 79 (the panel at 18:25 is blurry and may read Flow about 84, Density about 68)
edits.reason: Darken the outer hills and clouds for depth

darktable_modules: exposure (several instances) with drawn gradient, ellipse and brush masks
examples.darktable_equivalent: Several exposure instances (or one per zone), each with drawn masks: gradients for the edge burns, an ellipse behind the trees combined with a parametric sky mask, and brush masks (hardness ~0, opacity ~70%) for dodge (+0.4 EV) and burn (-0.3 EV). Darktable brush masks have hardness/opacity rather than Flow/Density, and pressure settings approximate flow. The tone equalizer with masking can also do zone-based tonal shaping. B&W base: color calibration gray tab or monochrome.
